title: Birth and death: from cradle to grave
subtitle: conceive, go into labour, pass away, bequeath
summary: Talk about the beginning and the end of life with the right register - medical words for pregnancy and birth, and formal, informal and legal ways of talking about death.

lesson.heading: Pregnancy
lesson.text: **Pregnancy** is the nine-month period when a woman is expecting a baby. It begins with **conception**, when the mother's egg is **fertilised** and an **embryo implants** in the mother's **womb**, or **uterus** - uterus is the more medical word.

examples.text: Laila's **expecting** a baby - it's due in the middle of October.
examples.note: Expect in this sense is only used in the continuous form: they are both expecting, not ~~they both expect~~.

examples.text: Most mothers **conceive** naturally but some are helped by **fertility drugs** or by **IVF**.
The first **test tube** baby was born in 1978.
examples.note: IVF = in vitro fertilisation, which fertilises an egg in a laboratory

lesson.heading: The baby grows
lesson.text: From eight weeks onward the developing baby is called a **foetus**. It is fed through the mother's **placenta**, the organ connecting the developing baby to the mother and giving it food.

examples.text: During the nine months of **pregnancy**, the baby developing inside the mother is often referred to as a **foetus**.
The **placenta** provides the baby growing in the mother's **womb** with all the food it needs.
If Liz doesn't **conceive** soon, she's going to ask her doctor for a fertility test.

lesson.heading: The birth
lesson.text: After 40 weeks, the mother usually **goes into labour** - the last stage of pregnancy, where the womb pushes the baby out. If this does not happen naturally, she may be **induced**. A **midwife** helps the mother **give birth**; sometimes a surgeon **delivers** the baby by **caesarean section**.

examples.text: Karen went into **labour** at midnight and gave **birth** only four hours later.
Did Amy have a natural **delivery** or a **caesarean section**?
As well as helping with the birth, a trained **midwife** usually visits the mother before and after the birth.
Shona Harrison **gave birth to** twins last Monday.

lesson.heading: Growing old
lesson.text: To **live to a ripe old age** is to live well into old age. Your **late** father means your father who is now dead. A **pensioner** is an elderly person receiving a state pension, and **sheltered accommodation** is special housing, usually for old people, where care staff also live.

examples.text: All my grandparents lived to a **ripe old age**.
My aunt - that's my **late** father's sister - is 93.
She's been a **pensioner** for more years than she worked, and she lives in **sheltered accommodation**.
My neighbour is 90 but she still has all her **wits about her**.
examples.note: = she is still able to think and react quickly

lesson.note: Doddery (weak on the legs because of old age) is informal, and dementia is the illness that causes memory loss.

lesson.heading: Funerals
lesson.text: A **coffin** is the box where the dead person is put, and the **wake** is the gathering of family and friends after the funeral. **Mourning** is expressing sadness after someone's death; people who have lost someone have been **bereaved**. At a **cremation** the body is burnt at a **crematorium**; at a **burial** it is buried in the ground, and the **ashes** may be **scattered**.

examples.text: The whole country is in **mourning** after the President's death.
I'd like my **ashes scattered** in my favourite forest.
She'd put it in her **will** that her own ashes are to be sent up in a rocket!
Funerals now are often more about celebrating a person's life than just about **mourning**.

lesson.heading: Death in different registers
rows: I was so sorry to hear of your loss.
pass away, pass on, pass over
be at death's door, be on your last legs
be close to death (also used of machines)
the deceased, bequeath, inherit, die intestate
the dead person; leave in a will; receive from someone who has died; die without a will

lesson.heading: The legal words
lesson.text: You **bequeath** something to someone in your **will** (the noun is a **bequest**), and they **inherit** it (the noun is an **inheritance**). Someone who dies without making a will **dies intestate**.

examples.text: My father **bequeathed** me his gold watch in his will.
My aunt left me a **bequest** of £500 in her will.
John's three nephews each **inherited** £1,000 from him.
Unfortunately, the **deceased** died without leaving a will - he **died intestate**.

lesson.text: On your last legs is always plural, and at death's door - not window. Both are very informal.

exercises.prompt: If Liz doesn't ___ soon, she's going to ask her doctor for a fertility test.
exercises.explanation: To conceive is to become pregnant; the noun is conception.

exercises.prompt: Karen went into ___ at midnight and gave birth only four hours later.
exercises.explanation: To go into labour is to enter the stage where the womb pushes the baby out.

exercises.prompt: Did Amy have a natural delivery or a ___ section?
exercises.explanation: In a caesarean section the abdomen and womb are cut open so the baby can be removed.

exercises.prompt: The ___ provides the baby growing in the mother's womb with all the food it needs.
exercises.explanation: The placenta is the organ connecting the developing baby to the mother and giving it food.

exercises.prompt: The first test ___ baby was born in 1978.
exercises.explanation: Babies born through IVF are sometimes called test tube babies.

exercises.prompt: A trained ___ helps women when they are giving birth and visits the mother afterwards.
exercises.explanation: A midwife is medically trained to help women give birth.

exercises.prompt: Laila's ___ a baby - it's due in the middle of October.
exercises.explanation: Expect meaning expect a baby is used only in the continuous form.

exercises.prompt: From eight weeks onward, the baby developing inside the mother is called a ___.
exercises.explanation: The embryo is called a foetus from about eight weeks onwards.

exercises.prompt: All my grandparents lived to a ___ old age.
exercises.explanation: To live to a ripe old age is to live well into old age.

exercises.prompt: My neighbour is 90 but she still has all her ___ about her.
exercises.explanation: To have all your wits about you is to be still able to think and react quickly.

exercises.prompt: Please accept my ___ on the death of your mother.
exercises.explanation: Please accept my condolences is the formal expression; I was so sorry to hear of your loss is the informal one.

exercises.statement: The whole country is in morning after the President's death.
exercises.explanation: The word is mourning: The whole country is in mourning after the President's death.

exercises.statement: My extinct grandfather was a shepherd all his life.
exercises.explanation: Of a person we say late: My late grandfather was a shepherd all his life.

exercises.statement: I'm afraid her elderly step-mother has just passed off.
exercises.explanation: The euphemisms are pass away, pass on or pass over: her step-mother has just passed away.

exercises.statement: Mrs Wilson seems to have been at death's window for years.
exercises.explanation: The expression is at death's door: Mrs Wilson seems to have been at death's door for years.

exercises.statement: It was amazing there were no fatalities when the bridge collapsed.
exercises.explanation: Correct - fatalities is the newspaper word for people who have died in an accident or disaster.

exercises.prompt: My father ___ me his gold watch in his will.
exercises.explanation: You bequeath something to someone; they inherit it from you.

exercises.prompt: My aunt left me a ___ of £500 in her will.
exercises.explanation: A bequest is something left to someone in a will.
Perish is not used in the passive: over 2,000 people perished.

exercises.prompt: Unfortunately, the deceased died intestate. That means he died ___.
exercises.explanation: To die intestate is to die without having made a will.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: the box in which a dead person is put
the gathering of family and friends after a funeral
a service at which the body is burnt
what is left of a body after cremation
having lost someone close to you
housing for old people where care staff also live

exercises.prompt: Which register does each expression for dying belong to?

exercises.answer: Shona Harrison gave birth to twins last Monday
exercises.explanation: You give birth to a baby; the doctor or midwife delivers it.
